title: Sum of squared row-sums as a sum over column pairs
statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite types and let $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \bbr$. Then
\[
  \sum_{x \in \alpha} \Bigl(\sum_{y \in \beta} f(x,y)\Bigr)^2
  \;=\;
  \sum_{(y,z) \in \beta \times \beta} \; \sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x,y)\, f(x,z).
\]
That is, squaring each row-sum of $f$ and summing over rows yields the same value as summing, over every ordered pair of columns $(y,z)$, the inner product of those two columns.
hypotheses_covered: f is a real-valued function of two arguments f : α → β → ℝ
replaced:
For finite types $\alpha$ and $\beta$ and $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \mathbb{R}$,
\[
  \sum_{x : \alpha} \Bigl(\sum_{y : \beta} f(x, y)\Bigr)^2
  \;=\; \sum_{(y_1, y_2) : \beta \times \beta} \sum_{x : \alpha} f(x, y_1) \cdot f(x, y_2).
\]
